name: Backgammon
summary:
Backgammon is a two-player abstract board game of dice and movement. Two opponents share a board of twenty-four triangular points arranged in two facing rows of twelve. Each controls fifteen checkers that begin in four fixed stacks and travel the circuit in opposite directions, so that each player's path runs through ground the other is leaving or occupying. The aim is to gather every checker into the six-point home quadrant and then remove them all.

Play alternates, and each turn starts with two dice. Each die moves a checker that many points, either one checker for both values or two checkers separately; matching dice are used four times, and any legal use of both numbers is compulsory. A point holding two or more opposing checkers is closed. A lone checker, called a blot, is hit when an opponent lands on it and goes to the bar; it must re-enter in the opposing home board before any other move is allowed, and a roll with no legal entry is lost. Once all fifteen are home, checkers are borne off by die value. Whoever clears the board first wins one point, two for a gammon or three for a backgammon, multiplied by the doubling cube, which can be offered before a roll; the opponent then accepts or resigns.

Matches run to five points under the Crawford rule, with eight minutes per player plus ten seconds per move. Play is available online against people or against AI, alongside a tutorial, a ladder of solo games and a daily bear-off race with shared dice.
